lastCompletedStory.title: cam plan / next / ship refuse the signal-write when the sidecar is dead

nextStoryContext: US-003 added a shared `sidecarLivenessGate(claudeDir, cmdName, sidecarAliveFn?)` helper (new file src/commands/sidecar-gate.ts, defaulting sidecarAliveFn to sidecarAlive from src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts, US-002) and wired it into runPlan/runNext/runShip's existing liveness/mutex preamble, right after the paneCountMutex busy-check and BEFORE the phase:planning/active:true/phase:shipping state-file write. Each of PlanOptions/NextOptions/ShipOptions gained an injectable `sidecarAliveFn?: (claudeDir: string) => boolean` seam. The gate is mode-agnostic by construction (no worker_isolation branching in the gate itself), satisfying AC4 without any container-specific code path. Adding the gate call pushed runPlan's cognitive complexity over Biome's ceiling (17, then 16 after the shared-helper extraction); fixed with a SECOND, runPlan-specific extraction of the F-01 issue-resolution + state-file write into `resolveAndWritePlanningSignal(cwd, claudeDir, options)` (returns `string | null`). runNext/runShip did not need this second extraction (they had headroom). Every existing happy-path test in plan.test.ts/next.test.ts/ship.test.ts/attach-hint.test.ts that expects a successful write now injects `sidecarAliveFn: () => true` (the real default probes a real pid file at `<cwd>/.claude/.cam-sidecar.pid`, which is absent in every tmp-dir test fixture, so omitting the fake now makes the command refuse and return 1). Tests that already expected code 1 for an unrelated reason (mutex busy, bootstrap failure, marker timeout, missing pane) did NOT need updating, since they return 1 before ever reaching the new gate. New dedicated describe blocks ('runPlan: sidecar liveness gate', 'runNext: sidecar liveness gate', 'runShip: sidecar liveness gate') cover dead-refuses-no-write, alive-proceeds, and an AC4 mode-agnostic assertion (dead sidecar refuses regardless of any worker_isolation config, proven by the gate having zero config-read code path). File-size-budget.json raised 4 source ceilings + prd.json passes flip in the same commit; used a targeted single-story Edit for the prd.json passes flip (NOT python json.dump, which re-serializes the WHOLE file and mangles pre-existing non-ASCII characters like ⚠/— into \uXXXX escapes — caught and reverted before committing, worth flagging for any future story that reaches for a full-file JSON rewrite tool on prd.json).
